task: The user's own single, deliberately under-specified request: 'we need to work on publish quality. it can be high resolution.' No destination or exact degree was named; a clarifying AskUserQuestion (Export scope) went unanswered, so -- per this session's own standing instruction to proceed autonomously on an unanswered question rather than stall -- the recommended defaults from that question were shipped: Story Carousel bumped 2x resolution, Story Book Print-ready PDF bumped from a misleadingly-labeled 216 DPI to true 300 DPI, Story Book Digital PDF left completely unchanged (already screen-optimized). Disclosed here for the user to confirm or redirect, not silently assumed as final. Root cause, confirmed by direct code read: js/storyDestinations.js's shared _renderSlideInto(canvas, slide, idx, total, opts) unconditionally called SlideRenderer.init(mid, {dpr:1, adaptiveViewport:true}) regardless of how much larger the destination canvas actually was -- so the old Print-ready PDF (nominally 216 DPI, 1620x2025) was never a genuinely sharper render, only a 1080x1350-quality image stretched up via _fitCompositeInto's own smoothing, no crisper than the Digital PDF underneath it. SlideRenderer.init's dpr option already exists specifically to produce a genuinely higher-density NATIVE render -- the fix was threading a real scale value into it, not inventing new rendering machinery. Fix: _renderSlideInto gained an opts.scale parameter (default 1, so every unspecified caller is byte-for-byte unaffected) passed straight through as SlideRenderer.init's dpr; BOOK_FORMATS.print gained a renderScale field and its dimensions were corrected to genuinely reflect true 300 DPI (2250x2813, replacing the old 1620x2025), with BOOK.renderPage reading ctx.format.renderScale and passing it through; CAROUSEL_RENDER_SCALE=2 was introduced and CAROUSEL_FORMATS' Portrait/Square dimensions doubled (2160x2700 / 2160x2160, up from 1080x1350 / 1080x1080), with CAROUSEL.createCanvas/.renderPage both using the new scale. Verified via a decisive, byte-level Playwright test driving the REAL Publish Studio UI through all 4 format combinations and decoding the actual downloaded file's own metadata directly -- a PDF's /Width N /Height N dictionary token and a PNG's IHDR chunk (byte-parsed) -- rather than trusting the UI alone: Digital PDF confirmed unchanged at 1080x1350; Print-ready PDF confirmed genuinely 2250x2813 (a real 152,501-byte file); Carousel Portrait confirmed genuinely 2160x2700; Carousel Square confirmed genuinely 2160x2160 with real, non-blank rendered content (a 1.7MB PNG). Since Studio ships with zero built-in themes today and Supabase is unreachable in this sandbox, the test seeds the real, already-validated themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme file directly into localStorage and drives through 'Showcase My Artwork' -- the same, already-proven pattern this session's own welcome_heading_removed_verify.js established. Full regression: confirmed via git diff --stat that only js/storyDestinations.js changed; a full scratchpad grep for any other script asserting the old Carousel/Print resolution values found exactly one, verify_rotation_publish_honored.js -- its one hardcoded canvasW===1080 Carousel-size assertion was the disclosed, intended consequence of this fix, corrected to 2160x2700 and re-verified 10/10 passing, confirming Rotation-reaching-real-Publish-output is completely unaffected by the resolution change. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; tools/world-builder/ and tools/world-builder-v2/ are untouched -- confined entirely to js/storyDestinations.js.
